content.title: About
content.content: Soft pretzels are a ready‑to‑eat, unsalted, butter‑free baked snack made from wheat flour, water, yeast and a pinch of salt. They have a mild flavor and a chewy texture, perfect for pairing with a variety of dips and toppings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soft pretzels originated in Germany, where they are known as "Brezel".
The iconic twisted shape is said to represent crossed arms in prayer.
In the United States they are commonly served with mustard, cheese sauce, or sweet glazes.
There are more than 200 pretzel varieties, including chocolate‑filled, cinnamon‑sugar, and nut‑topped versions.
Sales of ready‑to‑eat soft pretzels in Europe grew by over 12 % in the early 2020s.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Provides quick‑digesting carbs for an immediate energy boost.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Absence of butter makes them less calorie‑dense than many baked snacks.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour supplies modest amounts of thiamine, riboflavin and niacin, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Plant protein
items.content: Each serving delivers about 5 g of protein, helping to promote satiety.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Soft texture is gentle on the digestive system, suitable for children and seniors.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Made from wheat flour, they are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Although unsalted, a small amount of sodium may be present in the recipe.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Can raise blood sugar quickly, so portion control is advised for diabetics.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy soft pretzels as a snack on their own, split them and spread with cream cheese, hummus, avocado, or sweet jam. They also serve as a base for mini sandwiches and appetizer bites.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3‑4 days. For longer freshness, store in the refrigerator, where they stay soft for about a week.
